\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{راهنمایی} \fa{کردن} (râhnamâyi kardan)}{راهنمایی کردن (râhnamâyi kardan)}]{\fa{راهنمایی} \fa{کردن} (râhnamâyi kardan) — to give directions, to guide}

\label{lesson:FA-C144-rahnamayi-kardan}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for to fill, then the Persian for to hand in.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{راهنمایی} \fa{کردن}}
\textbf{\fa{راهنمایی} \fa{کردن}} — \emph{râhnamâyi kardan} — \textquotedblleft{}to give directions, to guide\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{râhnamâyi kardan} pairs \emph{râhnamâyi}, \textquotedblleft{}guidance\textquotedblright{}, with \emph{kardan}. \emph{râhnamâyi} is \emph{râh}, \textquotedblleft{}road\textquotedblright{}, with \emph{namâ}, \textquotedblleft{}showing\textquotedblright{} (from \emph{nemudan}, \textquotedblleft{}to show\textquotedblright{}), and \emph{-i}: road-showing. All the pieces are native Persian. \emph{kardan}, \textquotedblleft{}to do\textquotedblright{}, is an inherited verb, from Middle Persian \emph{kardan} (EtymDB).
\end{cousinweb}

  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Persian for to fill, then the Persian for to hand in, then say \emph{râhnamâyi kardan} again
\end{itemize}
